I am 62 years old and have farmed these lands in Quzhou County for 40 years. With the schooling I received, I have always paid close attention to what the extension agents and my own experience teach me. My household is just my wife and me, and our farm is 8 mu — not large, but manageable for two people if we work smart. We have a reliable well, which is a blessing on the North China Plain.

Our land is all under the wheat–maize rotation. I will plant the full 8 mu to winter wheat this autumn, harvest it in early June, and immediately sow summer maize on the same 8 mu. This is the system that feeds our household and gives us grain to sell.

For **winter wheat**, I will use an **improved** semi-dwarf variety such as the Jimai or Lunxuan lines that have done well here. I will do **rotary tillage** before sowing to prepare a fine seedbed. I have learned that balanced fertility is key, so I will apply about **16 kg of nitrogen, 8 kg of phosphorus, and 6 kg of potassium per mu**, using a compound fertilizer as base dressing and urea as topdressing at the jointing stage. With our well, I can irrigate four times: after sowing, at the returning-green stage, at jointing, and during grain filling. I will spray pesticides four times in total — a herbicide at sowing or early spring, plus fungicide and insecticide sprays to protect against rust and aphids.

For **summer maize**, I will sow a **hybrid** variety immediately after wheat harvest. Time is short, so I will use **no-tillage** seeding, which also saves fuel and preserves soil moisture. I will apply **16 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu**, placing fertilizer at sowing and side-dressing urea at the big-trumpet stage. I will irrigate three times — at sowing if the soil is dry, at the big-trumpet stage, and at grain filling. I will spray three times: a herbicide and two insecticide applications to control corn borer and armyworm.

I expect the wheat to yield about **520 kg per mu** and the maize about **620 kg per mu**, which is what I usually achieve when the weather cooperates and I manage carefully.
